title: SQL Server change tracking at 150 tables: every table is read about every 17 s

found.by: 2026-10-26 rerun: SQL Server 2022 CU27-GDR, change tracking, 150 one-row tables in one gateway; a new key inserted every 2 s into one table for 10 min, then into another; a control table and 10 idle tables at one insert per minute

symptom: All 631 inserted rows were staged, with no table starved, but a table changed every 2 s was read every 16.6-18.5 s (36 reads in 10 minutes, up to 10 rows a read). Lag from commit to the gateway's staged change: p50 11-12 s, max 20 s, for busy, control and idle tables alike.
cause: Not isolated. Reads of different tables fall a few seconds apart, consistent with one pass over all 150 tables taking about 17 s; the per-table wait in the scheduling code (1-5 s at 150 tables) is a floor, not a bound on the pass.
effect: With many tables in one gateway, a change can take 20 s or more to reach staging, even on a busy table.
fix: None tested. To measure it, insert a new key per change and read the staging change files' extraction times; compare at other table counts before splitting pipelines.
notes: Supersedes the round-2 reading that a busy table was starved: that load updated one row (id = 1) each time, and change tracking returns one net change per key between reads. One run at one table count.
